From 1badfc4319224820d5d890f8eab6aa52e4e83339 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
Date: Mon, 6 Apr 2026 16:03:25 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] HID: alps: fix NULL pointer dereference in alps_raw_event()

Commit ecfa6f34492c ("HID: Add HID_CLAIMED_INPUT guards in raw_event
callbacks missing them") attempted to fix up the HID drivers that had
missed the previous fix that was done in 2ff5baa9b527 ("HID: appleir:
Fix potential NULL dereference at raw event handle"), but the alps
driver was missed.

Fix this up by properly checking in the hid-alps driver that it had been
claimed correctly before attempting to process the raw event.

Fixes: 73196ebe134d ("HID: alps: add support for Alps T4 Touchpad device")
Cc: stable <stable@kernel.org>
Cc: Jiri Kosina <jikos@kernel.org>
Cc: Benjamin Tissoires <bentiss@kernel.org>
Cc: Masaki Ota <masaki.ota@jp.alps.com>
Cc: linux-input@vger.kernel.org
Assisted-by: gregkh_clanker_t1000
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
Signed-off-by: Jiri Kosina <jkosina@suse.com>

diff --git a/drivers/hid/hid-alps.c b/drivers/hid/hid-alps.c
index 21e55f3d0d1b..67179e3fe39b 100644
--- a/drivers/hid/hid-alps.c
+++ b/drivers/hid/hid-alps.c
@@ -437,6 +437,9 @@ static int alps_raw_event(struct hid_device *hdev,
 	int ret = 0;
 	struct alps_dev *hdata = hid_get_drvdata(hdev);
 
+	if (!(hdev->claimed & HID_CLAIMED_INPUT) || !hdata->input)
+		return 0;
+
 	switch (hdev->product) {
 	case HID_PRODUCT_ID_T4_BTNLESS:
 		ret = t4_raw_event(hdata, data, size);
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of the Patch

The patch fixes a NULL pointer dereference bug in the `alps_raw_event()` function of the HID Alps driver (`drivers/hid/hid-alps.c`).

### Changes in `drivers/hid/hid-alps.c`

- **Added an early return guard** in `alps_raw_event()`:
  ```c
  if (!(hdev->claimed & HID_CLAIMED_INPUT) || !hdata->input)
      return 0;
  ```
  This checks whether the HID device has been properly claimed for input (`HID_CLAIMED_INPUT`) and whether the associated input device (`hdata->input`) has been initialized. If either condition fails, the function returns immediately with 0, preventing a NULL pointer dereference when attempting to process raw events.

### Relationship

- The modification ensures that the driver follows the safety pattern already applied to other HID drivers (e.g., `appleir`) that check for proper input claim before handling raw events. This pattern was previously missed in the Alps T4 Touchpad support, leading to a potential crash when raw events are received without the input device being set up. The added guard closes this gap and aligns the driver with the rest of the HID subsystem.

Here is the root cause:
The alps_raw_event() function does not check whether the HID device has been claimed for input (HID_CLAIMED_INPUT) or whether the input device (hdata->input) has been initialized, leading to a NULL pointer dereference when raw events are processed before proper input setup.

Here is the patch:
 
 static int alps_raw_event(struct hid_device *hdev,
 		struct hid_report *report, u8 *data, int size)
 {
 	int ret = 0;
 	struct alps_dev *hdata = hid_get_drvdata(hdev);
 
+	if (!(hdev->claimed & HID_CLAIMED_INPUT) || !hdata->input)
+		return 0;
+
 	switch (hdev->product) {
 	case HID_PRODUCT_ID_T4_BTNLESS:
 		ret = t4_raw_event(hdata, data, size);
 		break;
 	default:
 		ret = u1_raw_event(hdata, data, size);
 		break;
 	}
 	return ret;
 }
